newsitem.title: SPAIN: Asturiana secures valuable partner in Glencore.
newsitem.headline: Asturiana secures valuable partner in Glencore.

text.p: Spanish zinc producer Asturiana has secured a valuable partner in the global metals arena with Glencore but its share price is unlikely to benefit in the short term, analysts said on Wednesday.
Spain's stock market watchdog the CNMV gave Swiss commodities house Glencore the green light on Tuesday to purchase a 20 percent stake in Asturiana, bringing its total holding to 44.79 percent.
"Asturiana is now firmly in the hands of one of the main players in the world with a lot of expertise and this is bound to benefit the zinc producer in the long run," said a Madrid-based analyst.
However, analysts said Asturiana's share price was unlikely to draw strength from the deal in the short term although it would benefit from the positive evolution of zinc prices.
"The zinc cycle is in its favour and we are going to see rises," said Fabian Ramon, equity analyst at Ahorro Corporacion.

Glencore's purchase consolidates its position as Asturiana's main shareholder. Glencore already held 24.79 percent of the Spanish producer which it bought from the Banesto banking group in February for 1,820 pesetas a share.
The commodities giant offered almost twice as much for the additional 20 percent stake of 3,400 pesetas a share. On Wednesday Asturiana was trading 35 pesetas up at 3,300.
"I wouldn't take (Glencore's) offer as a hint of the fair value of the share," Ramon said however.
Although Ramon believed the share price was already 20 percent overvalued, he said it would outperform in the short term spurred by rocketing zinc prices.
Zinc prices have soared to seven-year highs this week boosted by news that beleaguered Chinese smelters are holding huge loss-making short positions in zinc.
The three-month zinc price hit a high of $1,674 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange on Monday. Despite collapsing to low of $1,370 on Tuesday prices had resumed their rise on Wednesday.
Some analysts said Glencore's purchase would stifle the liquidity of Asturiana's shares and could threaten its position in Spain's Ibex-35 index of leading shares.

"Investors should consider the possibility that Asturiana might lose its very recently acquire Ibex-35 status in the future through lack of liquidity, which in turn, could have an impact on prices," a Madrid-based analyst said in a recent note.
Asturiana joined the Ibex-35 in the bi-annual shake-up of the index in June. Liquidity is a key criteria for the index.

In the long run, however, Asturiana will profit from Glencore's position as one of the world's biggest commodity traders and its emergence as one of the big players in the global zinc market, analysts said.
Glencore recently also purchased stakes in a number of mining and refining groups, including France's Metaleurop and Peru's Iscaycruz.
Some analysts said they had upwardly revised their profit forecasts for Asturiana based on the soaring zinc prices and an ever stronger dollar.

Asturiana posted a net attributable loss of 2.65 billion pesetas in 1996 largely based on a loss-making futures position which it cleared. It said it expected to swing to profit in 1997 and post a net attributable profit of 5.0 billion pesetas based on an average zinc price of between $1,050 and $1,030 per tonne.
One analyst said that on a recent visit to the company the management had stated that 1997 results should be slightly below 10 billion pesetas.
For 1998, based on an average zinc price of $1,550 and an exchange rate of 147.5 pesetas to the dollar, net profit could be more in the region of 15 billion pesetas, one analyst said.
